newsitem.title: USA: BPA links higher prices to weather-related demand.
newsitem.headline: BPA links higher prices to weather-related demand.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) decided to raise firm peak power prices for Thursday because of cooler regional weather and early demand from utilities, the federal agency said Wednesday.
"The weather is getting colder so we have less surplus capacity," a BPA trade source explained.

"A couple of utilities called before we even posted our offer today looking for 16-hour blocks. We haven't been able to sell that lately so (the early buying interest) was a good indication of higher demand," he added.

Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest are forecast to average 2 to 6 degrees F above normal through Friday, dropping to near normal by the weekend when a rainstorm is expected to arrive, according to Weather Services Corp.
But Northwest market sources noted evening temperatures have been getting progressively colder, leading to a tighter balance of power supplies.
